specialist_trace.rationale: The documentation must explicitly state whether the metabolic acidosis and positive ketones represent diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a different acidosis etiology, and clarify if the type 2 diabetes is with or without ketoacidosis. Additionally, specify the diabetes type based on clinical context (e.g., type 1, LADA, or type 2) given the acute onset and ketoacidosis, to ensure accurate coding reflects the true clinical picture.

Based on the chart, the metabolic acidosis (pH 7.30, HCO3 16) with positive ketones meets the diagnostic criteria for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), regardless of the documented type 2 diabetes label. Literature supports that DKA can occur in type 2 diabetes (ketosis-prone type 2 diabetes), but the acute onset and severe hyperglycemia (HbA1c 11.2%) also raise suspicion for type 1 diabetes or LADA, which requires autoantibody testing (e.g., GAD, IA-2) to clarify the diabetes type (PMID: 30733589; PMID: 30291106).
